title: Cluster 02 DRILL: Dihybrid Crosses, Linkage and Epistasis
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 6 · 11 questions · 76 marks · 34 parts · six full genetic diagrams, so budget an hour and three quarters, not 76 minutes · every question is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

The mark-a-minute rule under-counts this drill badly. Six of these questions ask you to lay out a full genetic diagram, and a four-mark diagram written properly, with the key, the two phenotype rows, the two genotype rows, the circled gametes, the random fertilisation line, the labelled square and the two ratios, takes eight to ten minutes and not four. Set aside an hour and three quarters, or run it in two sittings.

This is the load-bearing cluster of Book 6. LO 2(x) is the outcome the whole Book is built around and it says dihybrid crosses. Everything Cluster 1 did with one gene arrives here with two. Genetic diagram construction, ratio prediction and reverse inference together are , and all three live here.

Question 1 is the anchor. It is 9477 Specimen Paper 2 Question 4, parts (a) and (b), the only extended Book 6 question that exists on an official paper. Four of its eleven marks are for the diagram alone, and the stem hands you the ratio before you start. You are told the answer and paid to lay out the working. Question 6 is 9477 Specimen Paper 1 Question 18, the only clear Book 6 MCQ in existence, and its four options are the mechanisms LO 2(x) itself names.

One scope ruling to hold on to, because it saves hours. LO 2(aa) excludes the modified epistasis ratios in its own brackets: "knowledge of the expected ratio for various types of epistasis is not required; focus of this section is on problem solving." Your notes tabulate seven of them across two pages. No question in this drill turns on recalling one. Every epistatic ratio here is derived from the interaction the stem describes, and two of them, in Q7 and Q11, appear in no table anywhere. Chromosome mapping is gone too: linkage maps, map units, centimorgans, crossover value as a computed number and gene ordering all are not in the learning outcomes. Recognising linkage from data stays; converting it to a distance goes.

Four real figures, three questions figure-led. Book 6 figures are not micrographs, they are counts: offspring numbers, a pedigree chart, a Southern blot, a chromosome ideogram. Every figure is the real image from the paper it came from, not a redrawing.

What the marks reward. Use the symbols the question supplies and no others. Write linked genotypes in the two-line stick form, one chromosome's alleles above its homologue's, because a scheme penalises under MP2 and MP3 if linkage notation is not used, so one habit costs two marks. Circle your gametes and underline them to show linkage. Label which offspring classes are parental and which are recombinant. Never write a ratio without its phenotypes. In an epistasis answer, name the enzyme and the pathway step it blocks, because a scheme prints penalise once if no reference to enzyme, and never volunteer a subtype name, because reject recessive epistasis and reject recessive/dominant epistasis both appear in this the papers.

Cumulative over Cluster 1 and Books 2 and 3. Q2 needs independent assortment placed at metaphase I from Book 3. Q5(d) needs the kinetochore, non-disjunction and aneuploidy from Books 2 and 3. Q7 needs sex linkage and the allele key from Cluster 1, on a species where the male has no Y at all. Q8 and Q11 need the genotype-to-phenotype chain from Cluster 1 run twice, once per locus, with one run broken.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers as well as for duplicated labels. Q1 the whole 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 machine, forwards and backwards · Q2 why two genes assort independently, in the one accepted wording · Q3 what a test cross is for and what its counts tell you · Q4 a linked test cross laid out in stick notation, and why it deviates · Q5 spotting linkage on a blot, and saying it in a form the scheme accepts · Q6 the specimen's own four-way choice between the mechanisms of LO 2(x) · Q7 an epistatic ratio derived from a pathway in a species with no Y chromosome · Q8 epistasis through the enzyme, then the same epistasis with linkage switched on · Q9 two linked loci carried through a family · Q10 counting genotypes when only one sex crosses over · Q11 two different merges of the same 9 : 3 : 3 : 1. The six genetic diagrams require six different answers: Q1(a) is an unlinked selfed dihybrid, Q4(b) a linked test cross in repulsion, Q7(c) an epistatic cross with an X-linked locus in an XO species, Q8(a) an epistatic test cross, Q9(a) a linked cross fixed by a pedigree, Q11(a) a duplicate-gene self cross giving 15 : 1.

Nothing from Books 7 to 9, and nothing from Cluster 3. The chi-squared test, continuous and discontinuous variation, the environment's effect on phenotype and the three assumptions behind a predicted ratio are all Cluster 3 and none of them is needed here, including on the specimen maize question, whose parts (c) and (d) are held back for that drill.
